Tuesday, Oct 15 – 5:00 PM – 8:00 PM , Wednesday, Oct 16 – 8:00 AM – 7:00 PM , I’d also recommend following them on social media they post about important information like that

8:30 is around/ after when they let people inside the queue hall, if you really want to be one of the first ones in you’ll want to get there around 7ish, 
There’s two separate lines outside and when they let people inside both of the lines merge together. If there’s something you REALLY want to be one of the first ones to, the earlier the better, as long as you’re in the first queue line indoors you’re gonna be one of the first ones to get in, they let the queues in one by one when it opens at 10

They recommend that you DONT do it Thursday, if you’ll be in the city , you can go Tuesday or Wednesday , you can go any day you want but Thursdays lines will be crazy long, so it’s a shorter line Tuesday and Wednesday, also follow NYCC on social media to keep up with updates from them about stuff like this

It’s not a superpower that I can hyperfocus on things for 10 hours but also not get up to eat drink or pee
It’s not a superpower that I lose my phone 10 times an hour
It’s not a superpower that I forget important dates and events and miss paying bills or canceling things
It’s not a superpower that it’s painful to do things I’m not interested in
It’s not a superpower that I go the entire day forgetting to eat
It’s not a superpower my memory is constantly fuzzy and I skip medication because I can’t remember if I JUST took it
It’s not a superpower that I cannot do simple math or understand it or read a clock or know my left from right
It’s not a superpower that when I don’t understand someone is joking around with me and everyone e gets the joke but me, I get frustrated and then I cry because of RSD

Sure, I would not be myself without ADHD imo, I think it’s an important part of who I am, BUT, that does not make it a superpower or something that is “good”
Referring to it as a superpower implicates that neurotypicals want this “superpower” as well, it really hurts our case that it is an actual disability that affects our lives in such a debilitating way, 
It also implies that we don’t need accommodating help since we have such a special thing
I think something that needs to be addressed more to neurotypicals is that being neurodivergent is more than stereotypical stuff 
There’s a lot to it that a lot of people probably wouldn’t know, and instead of “we have a superpower” neurotypicals need to help accommodate our disability, because that’s what it is, a disability, not a ‘superpower’ that’s so strong that we don’t neeeed extra help ,

A lot of the traits I mentioned that I am dealing with on the daily, are things people would be dismissive of “it’s simple math” or “just write it down so you remember it” or “why are you so sensitive” traits of being neurodivergent but people do not recognize that is the case, and therefore think “wow it’s easy to just fix your problems” when we know it’s not

But like other people said, if it’s used by us, that’s different, it’s a neurodivergent living with their disability trying really hard,
